page: Microsoft Azure D192ds_v7 is a massive general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running up to 4.2 GHz, configured with 96 physical cores and two threads per core to deliver 192 dedicated vCPUs. The CPU features 480 MB of shared L3 cache, along with 48 KB L1 data cache and 2 MB L2 cache per core. It is paired with 768.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. High-speed local ephemeral storage is bundled with the instance, providing 11,339 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. The instance does not include dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional parallel processing capabilities alongside substantial memory throughput. Multi-core performance is firmly top tier, registering 190,542.4 in stress-ng multi-core and 148,222.23 in the overall PassMark CPU test. Instruction-specific capabilities are elevated by support for AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and Intel AMX (tile and int8), reflected by a top-tier PassMark extended instructions test score of 235,953.37 and an encryption score of 195,179.7. Read-only large block memory bandwidth reaches 677.36 GB/sec, while write operations reach 268.41 GB/sec. Data processing throughput is validated by multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 1,037.97 GB/sec, database operations scoring 34,547.24, and Redis SET throughput exceeding 250 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput reaches 158.23 GB/sec.

Cost efficiency is driven by the density of execution resources and the integration of substantial NVMe SSD storage within a single general-purpose footprint. By combining 192 dedicated hardware threads, 768.0 GB of memory, and over 11 TB of local NVMe storage, the D192ds_v7 minimizes distributed architectural overhead for scale-up architectures. Although single-core stress-ng performance falls into the middle tier, aggregate multi-threaded scalability compensates effectively. The primary operational tradeoff involves the lack of hardware GPU acceleration, meaning CPU-based text generation remains modest relative to specialized accelerators despite solid prompt evaluation figures.

This server is engineered for demanding enterprise deployments that demand immense scale-up compute alongside fast local scratch space. Primary workload fits include enterprise relational and in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, heavy multi-threaded ETL pipelines, data analytics, software build farms, and high-throughput static web serving fleets.
description: Microsoft Azure D192ds_v7 is a high-density general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 192 dedicated vCPUs derived from a 96-core Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 768.0 GB of system memory (4.0 GB per vCPU) and bundles 11,339 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs. Benchmark results position the server in the top tier for multi-core throughput, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 190,542.4, large-block uncached memory read bandwidth of 677.36 GB/sec, and Redis throughput of 250.73 million SET operations per second. Its hardware instruction set supports AVX-512 and AMX matrix acceleration. The D192ds_v7 delivers qualitative density efficiency for demanding enterprise databases, vast distributed caches, large-scale data transformation workflows, and high-concurrency static web serving systems.
